scope: Make the existing voice terminal write atomic and retryable without changing the workflow or cancellation row/null contract.

beforeAfter.before: A failed version update could commit before pending pointer cleanup failed; retries skipped cleanup once the version was terminal.
beforeAfter.after: Both statements execute in one D1 batch. Either write failing rolls back the batch and rejects; an already-failed version may still clear its own residual pointer.

beforeAfter.before: The method selected a version only by its globally unique id and live status, without the scoped organization guard.
beforeAfter.after: The version write and pointer cleanup are scoped to the organization; cleanup also matches the version owner, pending id and failed status.

preservedContracts: A row means this call changed a pending/generating version to failed. Repeated failed, completed and missing claims return null.
Repairing an already-failed residual pointer still returns null and does not overwrite the terminal error.
Completed versions awaiting promotion, newer pending pointers, user selections and selected voice data are preserved.
Database errors reject; the existing failure step owns retries. No new scheduler, error swallowing or provider retry was introduced.
The scoped DB factory remains lazy: building its method surface does not construct the ownership query.

productionCallSites.purpose: Cancellation; the only production consumer of row/null. Null remains cancelled:false.
Trigger failure and two zombie recovery paths; await the write but do not consume row/null.
Demoted result and onFailure cleanup; do not consume row/null.
Durable parent cleanup when the child did not take failure ownership.
Continue voice failure cleanup in the existing durable step; no subsequent consumer of row/null.

originalAssertionTreatment: No existing assertions were removed or weakened. The new test fixture was corrected to the real updateVoice signature and required standardClothing field; synthetic SQLite errors are unwrapped from Drizzle query causes only inside the test assertion helper. The organization-level character creator also requires a real actor id, so the final fixture inserts a ULID user and passes that id.
alternativeAssessment: Outer workflow catches cannot make two SQL statements atomic. Reuse the existing D1 batch and scoped DB method rather than copying the voice lifecycle into a new extension module.
compatibilityRisks: Upstream changes to voice status, row/null cancellation semantics, pending promotion ownership, organization scoping or D1 batch must be reviewed against both statements.
This is one necessary upstream DB integration point, not completion of the full frozen responsibility inventory.
newEvidence: Twelve real createTestDb cases cover pending/generating rollback and retry, first-write failure, residual failed-pointer retry, repeat semantics, newer claim, user choice, completed promotion, foreign organization and absent id.
A corrected test baseline reproduced five behavior failures before the production change.
The same expanded regression command passed all 21 files and 426 tests after the lazy factory correction; earlier failures remain recorded.
remainingActions: Review Storyboard existing status-read/write race and terminal skip notification behavior.
Review other lifecycle/failure hooks without mechanically changing historical best-effort policies.
Real Cloudflare replay/restart, Workerd HTTP, actual D1 multi-instance concurrency, provider, remote D1/R2, browser delivery and settlement remain unverified.
